# Minimal GRIB2 File Header
# File: minimal_buffer_underrun.grib2 (187 bytes)
# Purpose: Trigger buffer underrun vulnerability in GRIB2 parser
#
## Structure Summary
# Total Size: 187 bytes (99.6% reduction from full 5-121MB files)
# Format: GRIB2 Edition 2
# Discipline: Meteorological (0)
#
## File Layout (by byte offsets)
# 0-15:    Section 0 - Indicator (16 bytes)
#            - Magic: "GRIB" (bytes 0-3)
#            - Discipline: 0 (byte 4)
#            - Edition: 2 (byte 7)
#            - Total Length: 187 bytes (bytes 8-15, big-endian)
#
# 16-36:   Section 1 - Identification (21 bytes)
#            - Section length: 21 (bytes 16-19)
#            - Section number: 1 (byte 20)
#
# 37-103:  Section 3 - Grid Definition (67 bytes, claims 72!)
#            - Section length: 72 (bytes 37-40) *** LIES! ***
#            - Section number: 3 (byte 41)
#            - Source of grid definition: 255 (predefined) (byte 42)
#            - Grid points: 1 (bytes 43-46)
#            - Grid template: 0 (bytes 47-48)
#            - Template data: 55 bytes claimed, only 50 present
#            *** MISSING 5 BYTES - TRIGGERS UNDERRUN ***
#
# 104-137: Section 4 - Product Definition (34 bytes)
# 138-159: Section 5 - Data Representation (22 bytes)
# 160-165: Section 6 - Bitmap (6 bytes)
# 166-171: Section 7 - Data (6 bytes)
# 172-175: End Section - "7777" marker (4 bytes)
#
## What Was Removed from Full GRIB2 Files
# - Section 2 (Local Use): Often 100s of KB, not needed for bug
# - Extensive Section 7 data: Reduced from millions to 6 bytes
# - Section 8 (Repeating): Only for multi-message files
# - Most metadata fields in Sections 1, 4, 5: Simplified to minimum
#
## Why These Removals Were Safe
# The buffer underrun bug occurs specifically during Section 3 parsing.
# Only Sections 0-3 are read before the bug triggers, so sections 4-7
# are structurally required but not involved in the vulnerability.
# Section 2 and 8 are optional and not needed for basic parsing.
#
## Bug Trigger Mechanism
# 1. Parser reads Section 3 length field (bytes 37-40) = 72 bytes
# 2. Parser trusts this length claim without validation
# 3. Parser calculates Grid Definition Template size: 52 + Nx*Ny bytes
#    For this file: 52 + 1*1 = 53 bytes needed
# 4. Parser attempts to read template data (bytes 50-102 expected)
# 5. Reality: Section 3 only has 67 bytes total (ends at byte 104)
# 6. Result: Parser reads 5 bytes into Section 4 or hits bounds check
# 7. Error: TooShort { needed: 1, got: 0 } or undefined behavior
#
## Critical Byte Offsets for Underrun
# - 37-40: Section 3 length field (claims 72, should be 67)
# - 50-51: Grid Definition Template number (0 = Template 3.0)
# - 103-104: Last actual byte of Section 3
# - 104-105: First byte of Section 4 (parser shouldn't see this!)
#
## Expected Behavior
# When parsed, this file should trigger:
#   TooShort { needed: 1, got: 0 } error
# or memory safety check failure.
# If parsing succeeds, the bug has been fixed or file is corrupted.
#
## Verification
# Run: cargo run --example verify_minimal_underrun
# Expected output: "✓ Buffer underrun successfully triggered"
#
## Usage Notes
# This file is HAND-CRAFTED for testing. It is NOT a valid GRIB2 file
# in the sense that it contains intentional structural defects.
# Use only for controlled testing of buffer underrun vulnerability.
